title: How traffic reaches ZIA
aliases: how does traffic get to zia

prose.text: "How does this traffic get to ZIA?" splits into questions answered in order.

steps.label: Which methods exist, and which fits the site or user?
Tunnels from a site.
steps.text: GRE needs a static IP and has per-tunnel bandwidth limits: [[zia.traffic-forwarding.gre]], with health and failover in [[zia.traffic-forwarding.gre-failover]]. IPSec is the option for routers without GRE and for dynamic IPs: [[zia.traffic-forwarding.ipsec]], with its credential object in [[zia.traffic-forwarding.vpn-credentials]]. The static IP a GRE tunnel needs, and an IPSec VPN credential needs only for IP-based PSK, is [[zia.traffic-forwarding.static-ips]], and taking a data center's IPSec tunnels out of service for a period is [[zia.traffic-forwarding.dc-exclusion]].

steps.label: IPv6 clients.
steps.text: Which method carries IPv6, and what it needs, is [[zia.traffic-forwarding.ipv6]]; the NAT64 and DNS64 prefixes are [[zia.traffic-forwarding.ipv6-prefixes]].

steps.label: Special deployments.
steps.text: Azure Virtual WAN hubs are [[zia.traffic-forwarding.azure-vwan]]; China Premium Access, for organizations whose users work from mainland China, is [[zia.traffic-forwarding.china-premium]]; partner networks reached through Private Access are [[zia.traffic-forwarding.extranet]]; Citrix workloads are [[zia.traffic-forwarding.citrix-workloads]].

steps.label: Who resolves DNS for each method.
Is the traffic arriving, and at the nearest edge?

prose.label: Once the traffic arrives.
prose.text: How it learns the destination host (explicit versus transparent) is [[zia.proxy-mode]]; where ZIA sends traffic onward is [[zia.forwarding-control]]; how users are identified on each path is [[zia.authentication]]; which source networks are known is [[zia.locations]]; and how the firewall sees each path is [[zia.firewall.traffic-path]].
